measurement3_theRealDenominator.why: a sweep over token pairs is a HYPOTHETICAL denominator. A hover state is not a rendered state and axe does not scan one. So the pair sweep was discarded as a denominator and replaced with a DOM measurement.
measurement3_theRealDenominator.instrument: P:/tmp/k1-scan/probe.mjs. Serves this repo's own src/server.mjs on an ephemeral port, drives real Chromium through playwright-core, seeds the localStorage theme lever through addInitScript and ASSERTS document.documentElement's data-theme equals the requested theme before reading (an unapplied theme throws rather than being reported as a scanned theme), then for every element with a direct non-empty text child reads its computed color and walks its ancestors compositing every non-transparent background layer source-over until an opaque one is reached.
measurement3_theRealDenominator.countingRule: one row per (surface x theme x viewport x element-with-direct-text). The same element on two surfaces counts twice and on two viewports twice again. Elements inside a display:none ancestor ARE included, which axe skips, so these counts are a SUPERSET of axe node counts and are NOT comparable to them. The 4.5 / 3.0 threshold is chosen per element from its RENDERED size and weight, not assumed.

Leaving it is what keeps the fix provable here.

findingsSoFar.measured: web/shell.css:179 `.prov .sep { color: var(--sc-line-strong); }` renders a `|` character on the .prov chip's own --sc-surface-2 ground. Light #AEBAC5 on #F6F8FA = 1.855:1; dark #3B4854 on #18212A = 1.737:1. 874 elements per theme across all 23 surfaces, 167 of them in viewport, plus a further 46 per theme on a white/surface ground. findingsSoFar.whyNobodyHasSeenIt: axe puts the nav-foot .prov region in its INCOMPLETE bucket with reason elmPartiallyObscuring rather than in violations, because .nav-foot is position:sticky with an opaque background and axe will not composite through an overlap. So the failure is reported as 'cannot settle', an adjudication covers it at a ceiling of 1 node per theme, and the actual figure on this machine is 44 per theme.
findingsSoFar.correctionOwed: src/a11y-gate.mjs REVIEW_ITEMS[0] adjudicates that region as SUPPORTS on the basis that 'a person reads the footer text against a solid ground'. For the .sep children specifically that adjudication is refuted by direct computation: against the solid ground, at the declared token values, the glyph is 1.855:1 in light. The adjudication may still be right about the other children in that region; it is wrong about these. Quoted at source: src/a11y-gate.mjs:145 'SUPPORTS. web/shell.css gives .nav-foot position: sticky with an OPAQUE background (var(--sc-surface))...'
findingsSoFar.disposition: OUT OF SCOPE and routed. src/a11y-gate.mjs is G-99's file by dispatch. This is a token-consumer question (is --sc-line-strong an acceptable text colour, or should .sep be aria-hidden as the decoration it is) and is its own card.
findingsSoFar.recommendedFix: aria-hidden="true" on the .sep spans is almost certainly correct - a `|` between two data items is pure decoration and WCAG 1.4.3 exempts decoration - and it removes the nodes rather than recolouring them. That is a markup change in web/index.html, which G-100 owns this wave.
